sentences.text:
The petitioner is the accused in Crime No.5/2024 registered by the Cyber Crime Police Station,
Pathanamthitta, alleging the commission of offences punishable under Section 420 and 120(B) and read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 66D of the Information Technology Act.
2. By Annexure A1 order, the Court of the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Pathanamthitta, enlarged the petitioner on bail subject to the condition that he should surrender his passport within one week.

entities.text: Court of the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Pathanamthitta
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Subsequently, the petitioner filed Crl.M.P.No. 903/2025 to release his passport.
However, by Annexure A2 order, the learned Magistrate has dismissed the said application on the 2025:KER:85076 ground that there is every likelihood of the petitioner absconding.
Annexure A2 order is erroneous and unjustifiable.

Hence, the Crl.M.C.
3.
I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
4. The petitioner was enlarged on bail as early as on 11.11.2024.
It is nearly a year the petitioner has been scrupulously complying with the conditions.
In order to secure an employment abroad, he wants his passport to be released and he may be permitted to go abroad.
By Annexure A2 order, the learned Magistrate has dismissed the application on the sole ground that the petitioner likely to abscond.

5. It is well settled in Hussainara Khatoon v. Home Secretary, State of Bihar [(1980) 1 SCC 81], that onerous conditions like restricting the travelling of an accused shall not be restricted in a casual manner.

entities.text: Hussainara Khatoon v. Home Secretary, State of Bihar [(1980) 1 SCC 81]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Moreover, in Menaka Gandhi v. Union of India and another [AIR 1978 SC 597],
the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that the right to travel abroad is a fundamental right guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

entities.text: Menaka Gandhi v. Union of India and another [AIR 1978 SC 597]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. In light of the above exposition of law and the fact that the petitioner has been scrupulously complying with conditions in Annexure A1 order for the last one year, I am satisfied that the Condition Nos.(i) and (ii) in Annexure A1 order have to be deleted.
In the aforesaid circumstances, I allow the Crl.M.C. by deleting condition Nos. (i) and (ii) in Annexure A1 order order.

The learned Magistrate is directed to return the petitioner's passport to him, subject to the condition that he executes an undertaking before the Trial Court unconditionally Asif vs State Of Kerala on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75048348/
2 undertaking that he would appear before the Investigating Office as and 2025:KER:85076 when required and also appear for the trial.
